identity.name: Muddled Libra Rogue-VM Alert Storm — AI SOC Analyst Seven-Signal Incident-Grouping Validation (T1003.003 / T1550.003 / T1537)
identity.summary: Seven medium/low behavioral (ABIOC) alerts from one Muddled Libra rogue-VM intrusion — vSphere VM create, NTDS.dit-from-VMDK, ADRecon, gooner local admin, forged Kerberos tickets, Chisel 443 tunnel, and S3/Snowflake exfil — all within ~15h. The card validates whether XSIAM AI-triage collapses them into ONE correctly-summarized critical incident instead of an alert storm of seven.
identity.description: Muddled Libra (Scattered Spider / UNC3944 / Octo Tempest) runs low-malware, hands-on-keyboard intrusions and — per the Unit 42 operations playbook — repeatedly stands up a rogue virtual machine inside the target's own vSphere estate to work from a host that endpoint tooling does not watch. From that rogue VM the operator powers down virtualized domain controllers, mounts their VMDKs, and copies NTDS.dit + the SYSTEM hive off-disk (decrypted into 'result' and 'result.kerb'), enumerates AD with ADRecon (ComputerSPNs.csv), stands up a 'gooner' local-admin account, forges Kerberos tickets to move laterally over the SSH tunnel / RDP / PsExec, keeps a persistent SSH-over-HTTPS Chisel tunnel on 443 alive for ~15 hours, and attempts bulk exfiltration from Snowflake and to attacker S3 buckets. Each of those seven behaviors, scored in isolation by Cortex analytics, surfaces as a MEDIUM or LOW ABIOC — none is a single known-bad that trips a critical rule. The detection question this card exists to answer is NOT 'does any one signal fire' (they all do) but the F7 AI-triage question: does the XSIAM AI SOC analyst GROUP the seven correlated behavioral alerts into exactly ONE critical incident, on the same rogue host / attacker actor inside the ~15h window, and SUMMARIZE it correctly — naming the domain-controller compromise (NTDS.dit copied from the mounted DC VMDK) and the exfiltration channel (Chisel 443 tunnel + S3/Snowflake). The ground truth is one incident, not seven; a SOC drowning in an un-grouped alert storm is the failure mode. Seven ABIOCs model the seven signals, a correlation rule (CR-MP-0013) fuses them, a validation XQL surfaces the grouped evidence, and the terminal scenario step asserts the single stitched incident. This is the 'AI collapses the alert storm to one correctly-summarized critical incident' proof — the analytics/correlation depth a signature-per-alert SOC cannot reach.

campaigns: Muddled Libra rogue-VM hands-on-keyboard intrusions against enterprise vSphere / Active Directory estates (2024-2026)

prerequisites.description: Cortex XSIAM with the AI SOC analyst / alert-grouping capability enabled so correlated ABIOCs can be triaged into a single incident.

prerequisites.description: Cortex XDR / XSIAM agents and the vSphere, AD-audit, and NGFW ingestion feeds are live so the seven signal families reach xdr_data / esxi_syslog / ad_audit / panw_ngfw_traffic_raw / network_story.

payload.code:
# Non-destructive emitter for the seven Muddled Libra rogue-VM signal families.
# No real VM is created, no real NTDS hive is touched, no real data is moved:
# each stage drops a SAFE-MODE marker + a labelled log line the analytics/
# correlation layer keys on. Ground truth = ONE incident from these seven.
set -euo pipefail
BASE=/tmp/cortexsim-mp013
mkdir -p "${BASE}"
echo '[MP-013] signal 1/7: rogue vSphere VM created + local Administrator login'
touch "${BASE}/new-virtual-machine.SAFE-MODE"
echo '[MP-013] signal 2/7: NTDS.dit + SYSTEM hive copied from mounted DC VMDK (SAFE-MODE)'
touch "${BASE}/ntds.dit.SAFE-MODE" "${BASE}/result.kerb.SAFE-MODE"
echo '[MP-013] signal 3/7: ADRecon domain enumeration burst (ComputerSPNs)'
echo '[MP-013] signal 4/7: gooner local-admin account created (4720/4624 analog)'
touch "${BASE}/gooner-account.SAFE-MODE"
echo '[MP-013] signal 5/7: forged Kerberos ticket pass-the-ticket auth (RDP/PsExec lateral)'
echo '[MP-013] signal 6/7: Chisel SSH-over-HTTPS persistent tunnel on 443'
curl -s --max-time 5 "https://${STAGE_HOST:-127.0.0.1}:443/tunnel" -o /dev/null 2>/dev/null || true
echo '[MP-013] signal 7/7: bulk cloud exfil attempt to S3 / Snowflake (SAFE-MODE)'
touch "${BASE}/exfil-manifest.SAFE-MODE"
echo '[MP-013] expect XSIAM AI to GROUP these 7 medium/low ABIOCs into ONE critical incident'

input_variables.name: STAGE_HOST
input_variables.description: Authorised internal host the Chisel-tunnel-shape curl reaches during signal 6.

expected_artifacts.description: vSphere 'New Virtual Machine' creation event with a local Administrator login on the rogue host.
NTDS.dit + SYSTEM hive copied off a mounted DC VMDK, decrypted into 'result' / 'result.kerb'.
New local-admin account 'gooner' (Windows 4720) followed by an interactive logon (4624).
Persistent SSH-over-HTTPS Chisel tunnel to an attacker-associated destination on TCP 443, sustained for hours.

cleanup.code: rm -rf /tmp/cortexsim-mp013; echo '[CortexSim] SIM-MP-013 cleanup complete — SAFE-MODE markers removed.'

iocs.context: chisel.exe — SSH-over-HTTPS tunneling tool delivered inside goon.zip from an attacker AWS S3 bucket; sustains the 443 C2 tunnel.
goon.zip — attacker tool archive (contains Chisel + tooling) staged on an AWS S3 bucket.
psexec.exe — Sysinternals PsExec used for lateral movement from the rogue VM.
s3browser-12-6-1.exe — S3 Browser client used to attempt exfiltration to an attacker S3 bucket.
ADExplorer64.exe — Sysinternals AD browsing tool used during Active Directory enumeration.

Destination IP associated with Dropbox, observed in firewall logs from the attacker's rogue VM (Unit 42). A cloud-storage endpoint seen in the attacker VM's egress — NOT the Chisel tunnel endpoint (the post names no IP for the unnamed attacker-controlled 443 Chisel C2).

abiocs.name: MP-013 Rogue vSphere VM Creation with Local Administrator Login
abiocs.description: A 'New Virtual Machine' is created in vSphere and immediately logged into with a local Administrator account — the rogue-VM tradecraft Muddled Libra uses to work from a host outside EDR visibility. Individually a medium behavioral signal; the ABIOC anchors it to the vCenter identity + source-host chain.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = esxi_syslog
| filter event_message contains "VmCreatedEvent" or event_message contains "New Virtual Machine"
| filter user_name = "Administrator" or user_name contains "administrator"
| alter agent_hostname = source_address
| comp count() as vm_creates by agent_hostname, esxi_host, user_name
| filter vm_creates >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, esxi_host, user_name, vm_creates
abiocs.causality_anchor: Learned vCenter administrative baseline -> anomalous VM-create + local-Administrator login on a new rogue host, anchored to the source-address / identity chain.

abiocs.name: MP-013 NTDS.dit Extraction from Mounted Domain Controller VMDK
abiocs.description: NTDS.dit and the SYSTEM registry hive are copied off a mounted (powered-down) domain-controller VMDK and decrypted into 'result' / 'result.kerb' on the rogue VM — full-domain credential theft that never touches a live DC's LSASS. The ABIOC anchors the file activity to the rogue-VM process lineage.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.FILE
| filter action_file_name in ("ntds.dit", "SYSTEM", "result", "result.kerb")
| filter actor_process_image_name in ("cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "esentutl.exe", "diskshadow.exe")
| comp count() as ntds_ops by agent_hostname, actor_effective_username
| filter ntds_ops >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, ntds_ops
abiocs.causality_anchor: Rogue-VM process lineage -> NTDS.dit / SYSTEM-hive file access outside any DC role, anchored to the host + identity that mounted the DC VMDK.

abiocs.name: MP-013 ADRecon Domain Enumeration Burst
abiocs.description: A PowerShell ADRecon run enumerates the domain — forest, trusts, SPNs (ComputerSPNs.csv), users — in a short LDAP-heavy burst. Legitimate admins occasionally run AD reporting, so in isolation this scores medium; the ABIOC keys on the cadence + the rogue-host origin.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name = "powershell.exe"
| filter action_process_command_line contains "ADRecon" or action_process_command_line contains "ComputerSPNs"
| comp count() as adrecon_runs by agent_hostname, actor_effective_username
| filter adrecon_runs >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, adrecon_runs
abiocs.causality_anchor: Rogue-host PowerShell lineage -> ADRecon domain-enumeration burst (ComputerSPNs), anchored to the same actor that extracted NTDS.dit.

abiocs.name: MP-013 Rogue Local Administrator Account Creation (gooner)
abiocs.description: A new local account 'gooner' is created (Windows 4720) and immediately used for an interactive logon (4624) on the rogue host — attacker-controlled persistence. Account creation is routine in isolation (low), so the value is the correlation into the wider chain.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = msft_windows_security
| filter event_id in (4720, 4624)
| filter target_user_name = "gooner"
| alter agent_hostname = host_name
| comp count() as account_events by agent_hostname, target_user_name
| filter account_events >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, target_user_name, account_events
abiocs.causality_anchor: New local-admin account creation (4720) -> immediate interactive logon (4624) on the rogue host, anchored to the same host + attacker session.

abiocs.name: MP-013 Forged Kerberos Ticket Pass-the-Ticket Authentication
abiocs.description: Kerberos service tickets requested with RC4 (0x17) encryption — a downgrade consistent with tickets forged/roasted from the credential material harvested off the DC VMDK — are used for pass-the-ticket authentication, enabling RDP / PsExec lateral movement without re-entering passwords. The ABIOC keys on the RC4-downgraded 4769 service-ticket request (excluding the krbtgt TGT service) from the rogue host, normalized to the resolved endpoint entity (agent_hostname), rather than on all Kerberos traffic.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = ad_audit
| filter event_id = 4769 and ticket_encryption_type = "0x17"
| filter service_name != "krbtgt"
| alter agent_hostname = client_address
| comp count() as ticket_events by agent_hostname, service_name
| filter ticket_events >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, service_name, ticket_events
abiocs.causality_anchor: Harvested DC credential material -> RC4-downgraded forged Kerberos service ticket requested from the rogue host -> RDP/PsExec lateral movement, anchored to the resolved endpoint entity (agent_hostname).

abiocs.name: MP-013 Chisel SSH-over-HTTPS Persistent C2 Tunnel
abiocs.description: A Chisel SSH-over-HTTPS tunnel to an attacker-associated destination stays alive on TCP 443 for hours — protocol-on-non-standard-port persistence that blends into HTTPS. The ABIOC keys on the long-lived ssh-app-over-443 session from the rogue host.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter dest_port = 443 and app = "ssh"
| filter session_duration >= 3600
| alter agent_hostname = source_address
| comp count() as long_tunnels, sum(bytes_total) as tunnel_bytes by agent_hostname, dest_address
| filter long_tunnels >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, dest_address, long_tunnels, tunnel_bytes
abiocs.causality_anchor: Rogue host -> long-lived ssh-application session tunneled over TCP 443 to an attacker-associated destination, anchored to the source-host network profile.

abiocs.name: MP-013 Bulk Cloud Exfiltration to S3 and Snowflake
abiocs.description: The rogue host attempts bulk data movement to Snowflake and attacker AWS S3 buckets over 443 (via the S3 Browser client). Cloud upload volume alone is a medium behavioral signal; the ABIOC anchors the egress spike to the same host that dumped NTDS and forged tickets.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = network_story
| filter dest_host contains "s3" or dest_host contains "snowflake" or dest_host contains "amazonaws"
| filter action_total_upload_size >= 10000000
| comp sum(action_total_upload_size) as exfil_bytes by agent_hostname, dest_host
| filter exfil_bytes >= 10000000
| fields agent_hostname, dest_host, exfil_bytes
abiocs.causality_anchor: Rogue host -> bulk upload spike to S3 / Snowflake cloud destinations, anchored to the same actor that harvested and staged the domain credentials.

xql_queries.name: MP-013 Seven-Signal Incident Grouping Evidence
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 54000)
| filter actor_effective_username in ("Administrator", "gooner")
| comp count_distinct(action_process_image_name) as distinct_actions, count() as signal_events by agent_hostname
| filter signal_events >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, distinct_actions, signal_events

correlation_rules.name: Muddled Libra Rogue-VM Intrusion — Seven-Signal AI-Triage Incident Grouping
correlation_rules.logic: ABIOC(MP-013 Rogue vSphere VM Creation with Local Administrator Login) AND ABIOC(MP-013 NTDS.dit Extraction from Mounted Domain Controller VMDK) AND ABIOC(MP-013 ADRecon Domain Enumeration Burst) AND ABIOC(MP-013 Rogue Local Administrator Account Creation (gooner)) AND ABIOC(MP-013 Forged Kerberos Ticket Pass-the-Ticket Authentication) AND ABIOC(MP-013 Chisel SSH-over-HTTPS Persistent C2 Tunnel) AND ABIOC(MP-013 Bulk Cloud Exfiltration to S3 and Snowflake) within 54000s on the same resolved endpoint entity (agent_hostname — every ABIOC projects it; hostname-native bodies emit it directly, IP-native bodies (vSphere source_address, Kerberos client_address, NGFW source_address) normalize their raw identifier into it, and XSIAM XDM endpoint entity resolution reconciles hostname<->IP) -> fuse the seven medium/low behavioral alerts into ONE critical hands-on-keyboard-intrusion incident whose summary names the domain-controller compromise (NTDS.dit copied from the mounted DC VMDK) and the exfiltration channel (Chisel 443 tunnel + S3/Snowflake). Ground truth is one incident, not seven; the AI SOC analyst passes F7 when it produces a single correctly-summarized critical incident rather than an un-grouped alert storm.

use_cases.name: AI SOC Analyst Incident Grouping — Seven Signals to One Incident
use_cases.description: Cortex XSIAM's AI SOC analyst consolidates seven medium/low correlated behavioral alerts from a single Muddled Libra rogue-VM intrusion into one correctly-summarized critical incident, proving the analytics/AI-triage depth a signature-per-alert SOC cannot reach (F7).

test_cases.objective: The seven MP-013 ABIOCs fire and CR-MP-0013 groups them into exactly ONE critical incident on the rogue host, not seven separate alerts.
preconditions: vSphere, xdr_data, ad_audit, and NGFW feeds ingested for the rogue host.
steps: Emit the seven signal families from the same rogue host within the 15h window.
Let the correlation + AI-grouping layer converge.
Observe a single incident with all seven ABIOCs in its causality chain.
success_criteria: All seven MP-013 ABIOCs fire (medium/low individually).
CR-MP-0013 raises exactly ONE incident (count_distinct(incident_id) = 1) spanning the seven signals.
The grouped incident is scored critical.

test_cases.objective: The AI SOC analyst summary correctly names the domain-controller compromise and the exfiltration channel.
preconditions: TC-MP-013A produced a single grouped incident.
steps: Confirm it identifies the NTDS.dit-from-VMDK DC compromise and the Chisel/cloud exfil channel.
success_criteria: The summary names the DC compromise (NTDS.dit copied from the mounted DC VMDK).
The summary names the exfiltration channel (Chisel 443 tunnel and/or S3/Snowflake).

test_cases.objective: No alert-storm fan-out — the seven signals do not produce seven separate incidents, and triage-to-single-incident lands within the response-timing budget.
steps: Count incidents created from the seven ABIOCs.
Measure time from the last signal to the grouped incident.
success_criteria: Exactly one incident is created from the seven correlated alerts (not seven).
Time-to-grouped-incident is within the POV triage budget.

preventive_controls: Restrict vSphere/vCenter VM-create and datastore-browse permissions to a tiny admin set and require phishing-resistant MFA on vCenter — Muddled Libra's rogue-VM tradecraft depends on obtaining VM-create rights.
Alert on and block powering-down of domain controllers and mounting of DC VMDKs to non-DC hosts; treat DC virtual disks as crown-jewel assets.
Enforce phishing-resistant MFA and helpdesk identity-verification to blunt the social-engineering (vishing/smishing) initial access this actor relies on.
Egress-filter and inspect long-lived TCP 443 sessions; block Chisel-style SSH-over-HTTPS tunnels to non-sanctioned destinations.
detection_engineering: Let the XSIAM AI SOC analyst GROUP correlated behavioral alerts into a single incident rather than paging on each medium/low ABIOC — measure the seven-to-one consolidation and summary correctness, not just per-alert firing.
Alert on NTDS.dit / SYSTEM-hive file access on any host that is not a domain controller (the mounted-VMDK signature).
Alert on new local-admin creation (4720) immediately followed by an interactive logon (4624), and on forged/anomalous Kerberos tickets presented from hosts that never legitimately request them.
